t: You're at the tomb of Frederick Richards Leyland in Brompton Cemetery. Leyland was one of Britain's largest shipowners, running twenty-five steamships in the transatlantic trade. He was also a major art collector who commissioned work from several of the Pre-Raphaelite painters. The tomb itself was made by Edward Burne-Jones, the Pre-Raphaelite painter and designer, so it joins a patron and an artist from the same circle in one monument.
